members.algorithm: Use a best-fit priority that prefers the feasible bin with the smallest remaining capacity after placing the item, i.e. choose the maximum residual-capacity fit by returning `-(bins - item)`.
members.code:
def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return one priority for each feasible bin.

    ``bins`` contains remaining capacities after filtering bins that cannot
    hold ``item``.  The evaluator selects the first maximum priority and
    opens a new bin when the array is empty.
    """
    return -(bins - item)

members.algorithm: Both given algorithms score each feasible bin by a monotone function of its post-placement residual capacity `bins - item`, differing only in orientation: worst-fit maximizes it, best-fit minimizes it; the new rule uses a non-monotone, two-sided scoring that prefers bins whose residual capacity is near a target fraction of the item size, combining the useful spread of worst-fit with the tightness bias of best-fit.
members.code:
def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return one priority for each feasible bin.

    ``bins`` contains remaining capacities after filtering bins that cannot
    hold ``item``.  The evaluator selects the first maximum priority and
    opens a new bin when the array is empty.
    """
    post = bins - item
    # Prefer residuals near half the item size; penalize both very tight and very loose bins.
    return -np.abs(post - 0.5 * item)
